summary: Munish Chandra Joshi was an archaeologist and Indologist. He served as Additional Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (c. 1989-1990) and Member Secretary at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (c. 1997-2001).
Munkhjavkhlan Baatar is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who completed a PhD at the National University of Mongolia and held a post there.

Murray Barnson Emeneau, an Indologist and linguist, earned degrees at Dalhousie, Oxford, and Yale, studying under Franklin Edgerton, E. H. Sturtevant, and Edward Sapir. He taught at Yale (1926-1939) and UC Berkeley (1940-1971).

Murray Fowler was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Minnesota, Oregon, Vienna, and Harvard (PhD, under Joshua Whatmough). He held posts at Pomona, Purdue, Harvard, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1946-1953).

Musashi Tachikawa is an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher. He earned degrees at Nagoya and Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and held posts at Nagoya, the National Museum of Ethnology, and Aichi Gakuin University.

Muzaffar Alam is a historian and Indologist. He studied at Jamia Millia Islamia, Aligarh Muslim University, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, where he later taught (c. 1973-2001) before joining the University of Chicago in c. 2001.

Myles Dillon was a Celticist and Indologist. He studied at University College Dublin, Bonn, Berlin, and Heidelberg, and held professorships at Wisconsin-Madison, Chicago, Edinburgh, and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies, which he directed (1960-1968).
Myokyo-ni was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Graz and trained under traditional teacher Soko Morinaga in 1984.
Myosei Tatsuguchi is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts at Ryukoku University, serving as professor (attested 1987) and professor emeritus (attested 2015).

Mysore Hiriyanna was a scholar of Indian philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Madras Christian College, he taught at Government Normal School, Mysore, Maharaja's College, Mysore (c. 1912-1927), and the University of Mysore (c. 1917-1927).

Mysore Narasimhachar Srinivas was a sociologist and Indologist. Educated at Mysore, Mumbai (under G. S. Ghurye), and Oxford, he held posts at Oxford, Baroda, Delhi, the Institute for Social and Economic Change, and NIAS.

Mário Bruno Cruz is a translator and scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a master's degree at NOVA University of Lisbon and doctoral coursework at the University of Lisbon, working as an architect, translator, and reviewer.

Mélanie Vandenhelsken is a Tibetologist and religious studies scholar educated at Provence, Nanterre, INALCO, and Montpellier. She held positions at Montpellier, Namgyal Institute of Tibetology, Lille, and the University of Vienna.
Mónika Kiss is a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who pursued PhD studies at Eötvös Loránd University under the supervision of Masanori Yamaji.
N. A. Gore was an Indologist who served as librarian at the Asiatic Society of Mumbai (attested 1957-1958) and at Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar Marathwada University (attested 1967).

N. A. Jayawickrama was a scholar in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics who held professorships at the University of Ceylon (attested 1974) and the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies.

N. Aiyaswami Sastri was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Madras Sanskrit College and Visva-Bharati University. He held posts at Sri Venkateswara Oriental College, Sri Venkateswara Oriental Research Institute, and Visva-Bharati University.

N. D. Mironov was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg, Strasbourg, Berlin, Leipzig, and Bonn. He held academic posts at Moscow State University, the Asiatic Museum, Saint Petersburg, and Irkutsk State University.
N. J. Karthika is a scholar in computational linguistics and Indology who completed a PhD and held an academic post at the Indian Institute of Technology Bombay.

N. Lakshminarayana Rao was an Indologist and archaeologist who served as Government Epigraphist for India at the Archaeological Survey of India and as Special Officer (Epigraphy) for the Government of India in 1956.
